overview: In the Signature teaching of soldering basics, What Soldering Basics Studies is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Tinning means coating the iron tip with solder for heat transfer Cold joint means a dull grainy joint that will fail; reheat it Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Foundations material that follows.
core_concepts: Tinning: coating the iron tip with solder for heat transfer
Cold joint: a dull grainy joint that will fail; reheat it
key_laws: Heat the work, not the solder.
vocabulary: Cold joint: the dull cracked joint from moving parts during cooling
Wetting: solder flowing smoothly onto the metal, the sign of good heat
methods: Joint method: clean and tin the tip, heat the joint 2-3 seconds, feed solder to the joint, hold still while it cools
history: Soldering joined metals for millennia; electronics soldering standardized in the 1900s, and the maker movement of the 2000s taught a new generation with kits.
key_points: Tinning: coating the iron tip with solder for heat transfer
Cold joint: a dull grainy joint that will fail; reheat it
Key vocabulary: Cold joint — the dull cracked joint from moving parts during cooling; Wetting — solder flowing smoothly onto the metal, the sign of good heat.
Governing principle: Heat the work, not the solder.
